primitives.name: Pulse Waveform Processor
primitives.verbatim_quote: Pulse sensor based on photoplethysmography (optical measurement of blood-volume change in microvascular tissue) → ATmega8 microcontroller.
primitives.assumptions: PPG signal is periodic and linearly related to blood volume changes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Signal saturation or motion artifacts cause invalidation.

layer2.mapping: Maps raw optical sensor data into a time-series signal suitable for frequency domain analysis.
layer2.telemetry: Raw PPG waveform amplitude vs. time

primitives.name: Real-Time Heartbeat Tracker
primitives.verbatim_quote: The only "signal" mentioned is a real-time heart-rate value streamed to a web client, with tachycardia/bradycardia flagged when the measured rate deviates from a threshold.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'HR(t)': 'heart rate in beats per minute (BPM)', 'THRESH_HIGH': 'threshold BPM for tachycardia', 'THRESH_LOW': 'threshold BPM for bradycardia'}
primitives.assumptions: Heart rate is a deterministic function of PPG period and thresholds are fixed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Threshold crossing without physiological context leads to false positives.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a binary classification problem where HR(t) is mapped to abnormality flags.

primitives.name: Data Pipeline Gateway
primitives.verbatim_quote: The paper describes a data pipeline, not data collection: PPG sensor readings → UART serial → Bluetooth → Arduino → Ethernet → JSON messages → browser visualization.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D': 'data packet in bytes', 'T': 'transmission delay in seconds'}
primitives.assumptions: Data integrity is preserved through each transmission stage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Network congestion or hardware failure disrupts real-time delivery.

layer2.mapping: Represents a serial communication stack that transforms sensor data into network-deliverable JSON.

The core operators derive from a sequence of physical-to-digital transformations: PPG optical sensing → microcontroller sampling → serial communication → network delivery. Each step introduces noise and latency. The pulse waveform processor extracts a time-domain signal x(t) from raw optical intensity. The heartbeat tracker applies a threshold logic to map x(t) into discrete HR(t) values. The data pipeline gateway encapsulates these values into JSON packets for real-time visualization. Failure modes include sensor misalignment, signal aliasing, and communication bottlenecks. The system lacks statistical validation, so its reliability cannot be assessed quantitatively. The absence of labeled datasets or performance metrics precludes any meaningful modeling extension to GSE.
